reasoning: Traced the whole allocation path. FixWallGranOld's constructor calls the qualified 'FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)' (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:450) which allocates BOTH history_one and, when peratom_flag, array_atom (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1573). The Kokkos constructor then destroys history_one and calls the virtual grow_arrays again (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:44); every later growth goes through Atom::grow -> fix->grow_arrays(nmax) i.e. the Kokkos override (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:303-311), which grows only k_history_one and only 'if (use_history)'. array_atom therefore stays frozen at the initial atom->nmax. The base pack_exchange/copy_arrays that the Kokkos class delegates to still touch it: fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1584-1587 'array_atom[j][m] = array_atom[i][m];' and :1616-1619 'buf[n++] = array_atom[i][m];'. 'contacts' is a real keyword accepted by the shared constructor (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:410-413, peratom_flag=1, size_peratom_cols=8), so this is reachable with wall/gran/kk. Separately the constructor sets 'maxexchange = size_history;' (line 35) while FixWallGranOld::pack_exchange writes size_history+size_peratom_cols doubles, which undersizes both Comm::maxexchange_fix on the host path and the 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' grow in comm_kokkos.cpp:1371. And the device kernel never writes array_atom nor calls clear_stored_contacts(), which the CPU post_force does (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:637-639, 713-724), so the per-atom contact output is always zero.
fix: Simplest correct fix: reject the 'contacts' keyword (peratom_flag) in FixWallGranKokkos::init() with an explicit error, as is already done for fix_rigid. If it is to be supported: call FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays()/copy_arrays()/set_arrays() unconditionally for the array_atom part from the Kokkos overrides (they must run even when use_history is 0), set 'maxexchange = size_history + (peratom_flag ? size_peratom_cols : 0);' in the constructor, and have the kernel fill array_atom (plus a clear_stored_contacts equivalent).
